mechanism_comparison.standard_core: Factorial scaling is the natural q_n=n specialization of mixed-radix Cantor arithmetic, and an eventually stationary normalized rational sequence has a rational limit.
mechanism_comparison.local_delta: The source chooses the strict upper factorial-grid point Z_m=floor(m!P_m)+1 of the changing rational prefix P_m, proves its convergence after normalization, and obtains the exact recurrence b_m=mZ_{m-1}+1-Z_m. Rationality is then equivalent, in both directions, to eventual unit carries.
mechanism_comparison.integral_translation: The identity b_m=1 iff m divides Z_m turns the complete analytic endpoint into a cofinal finite divisibility predicate on exact rational prefixes.
mechanism_comparison.not_Engel: The construction is not naturally an Engel expansion: it does not present S as an Engel digit sequence with nested product denominators. Its closest standard home is factorial-radix/Cantor-series recurrence arithmetic.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: The reformulation is exact and strategically valuable, but it leaves the cofinal failure producer wholly unproved.
